message.content: {"skills": [{"category": "characterization", "trigger": "When evaluating pulmonary opacities on a chest X-ray to determine etiology based on margin definition and anatomical distribution.", "steps": ["Inspect the borders of the opacity to distinguish between well-defined (sharp, distinct margins suggesting consolidation or mass) and ill-defined (hazy, patchy, or ground-glass appearance suggesting interstitial or early alveolar process).", "Localize the opacity vertically within the lung fields (apex, mid-zone, or base/lower zone) by referencing rib levels and the diaphragm contour.", "Correlate the combination of ill-defined margins and lower/mid-zone predominance with viral pneumonias (e.g., COVID-19), whereas well-defined lobar opacities typically suggest bacterial pneumonia, and apical opacities suggest chronic conditions like TB or malignancy."]}]}
